exposure: COVID-19 infection in the second trimester
cohort: The cohort consisted of 369,887 mother-child pairs registered in the Prevention Agency-COVID-19-National Health Insurance Service (COV-N) in South Korea.
finding: The study found little evidence of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy affecting general maternal and neonatal outcomes, though a relationship between second-trimester infection and postpartum hemorrhages was discovered, and NICU admissions increased due to COVID-19 infection across all epidemic periods.
